Smart Dustbin
Automatic Open & Close

Build a touchless waste bin that senses a nearby hand, opens its lid, and automatically closes when the hand is gone. Explore the parts, adjust the budget, simulate the behavior, and copy the Arduino sketch.

Try the simulatorView parts and prices

How it works

  1. HC-SR04 detects a hand within approximately 20 cm.
  2. Arduino reads the measured distance.
  3. The servo rotates to open the lid.
  4. The lid stays open while a hand remains nearby.
  5. After five seconds without detection, the lid closes.

Project specifications

ControllerArduino UNO R3
SensorHC-SR04
ActuatorSG90 servo (light lid)
Detection threshold20 cm
Closing delay5 seconds
Suggested bin5–10 L, lightweight lid

SG90 is suitable only for a very light lid. Consider an MG996R with a suitably rated supply and stronger linkage for heavier lids. Arduino USB cable and mounting hardware may already be available in your classroom.

Exact pin connections

Component pinConnect to
HC-SR04 VCCArduino 5V
HC-SR04 GNDArduino GND
HC-SR04 TRIGArduino D10
HC-SR04 ECHOArduino D9
Servo signal (orange/yellow)Arduino D6
Servo +5V (red)External regulated +5V
Servo GND (brown/black)External supply negative
Arduino GNDExternal supply negative (common ground)
Power safety: Power the servo from a regulated external 5V supply; do not draw its motor current through the Arduino 5V pin. Connect Arduino GND to the supply negative. Power the Arduino separately via USB during initial testing. Never connect external 5V to an Arduino signal pin.

Detection controls

The sample Arduino code below uses fixed values (20 cm, 5 seconds). Changing these sliders affects the simulator only.

Arduino source code

Install the Servo library if your Arduino IDE requires it, select the Arduino UNO board and the correct COM port, then upload.

#include <Servo.h>

const int TRIG_PIN = 10;
const int ECHO_PIN = 9;
const int SERVO_PIN = 6;

const int DETECTION_DISTANCE = 20; // cm
const int CLOSED_ANGLE = 0;
const int OPEN_ANGLE = 90;
const unsigned long OPEN_DURATION = 5000;

Servo lidServo;
bool lidOpen = false;
unsigned long lastDetection = 0;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600);
  pinMode(TRIG_PIN, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(ECHO_PIN, INPUT);
  lidServo.attach(SERVO_PIN);
  lidServo.write(CLOSED_ANGLE);
}

float readDistance() {
  digitalWrite(TRIG_PIN, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(TRIG_PIN, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(TRIG_PIN, LOW);
  unsigned long duration = pulseIn(ECHO_PIN, HIGH, 30000);
  if (duration == 0) return -1;
  return duration * 0.0343 / 2.0;
}

void loop() {
  float distance = readDistance();
  if (distance > 0 && distance <= DETECTION_DISTANCE) {
    lastDetection = millis();
    if (!lidOpen) {
      lidServo.write(OPEN_ANGLE);
      lidOpen = true;
      Serial.println("Lid OPEN");
    }
  }
  if (lidOpen && millis() - lastDetection >= OPEN_DURATION) {
    lidServo.write(CLOSED_ANGLE);
    lidOpen = false;
    Serial.println("Lid CLOSED");
  }
  delay(100);
}

Build checklist

0 of 7 steps complete

Testing and troubleshooting

Lid does not move? Check D6, servo supply polarity, common ground, and mechanical linkage.

Arduino resets? Use an adequate regulated external servo supply; avoid powering the servo from the Arduino.

Sensor gives no readings? Verify TRIG D10, ECHO D9, VCC, and GND. Keep the sensor unobstructed.

Lid moves the wrong way? Adjust CLOSED_ANGLE and OPEN_ANGLE after testing the linkage without load.

Heavy lid? Use a stronger servo and proper mounting, rather than forcing an SG90.
